prompt: Company profile: Industrial coatings applicator in Elkhart, Indiana; 18 full-time employees; NAICS 332812 (metal coating and allied services). Situation: Annual purchasing records show the facility used about 28,000 pounds of toluene in coatings last calendar year, most of which evaporates during application and curing. The company has never filed toxics release reporting. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
# Compliance Obligations Register: Toluene Usage at Industrial Coatings Facility ## Executive Summary The facility's use of 28,000 lbs/year of toluene triggers **immediate, high-priority reporting violations** under EPCRA and creates multiple environmental, health, and safety compliance obligations. The company is currently non-compliant with federal emergency planning and community right-to-know requirements. --- ### **Obligation 1: EPCRA Section 313 – Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) Reporting** | Element | Details | |---------|---------| | **Requirement** | Submit EPA Form R (or Form A if eligible) for toluene by July 1 annually reporting all releases and other waste management activities. **Immediate action required:** File retroactive reports for prior years where thresholds were exceeded. | | **Regulatory Source** | 40 CFR 372; EPCRA Section 313 | | **Applicability** | **YES – OBLIGATION TRIGGERED**
• Toluene is a listed toxic chemical (CAS 108-88-3)
• "Otherwise used" threshold: **10,000 lbs/year** (facility used 28,000 lbs)
• Employee threshold: ≥10 full-time employees (facility has 18)
• NAICS 332812 is a covered industry sector | | **ISO 14001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Compliance obligations – environmental) | | **ISO 45001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Legal and other requirements – health impacts of toluene) | | **Evaluation (9.1.2)** | **How:** Track monthly toluene usage via purchase records and inventory; compare rolling 12-month total to 10,000-lb threshold. Calculate annual emissions using EPA emission factors or mass balance.
**When:** Continuous tracking with **formal evaluation by March 1** each year to prepare July 1 submission; immediate evaluation required now to determine retroactive reporting liability. | --- ### **Obligation 2: EPCRA Section 312 – Tier II Chemical Inventory Reporting** | Element | Details | |---------|---------| | **Requirement** | Submit annual Tier II chemical inventory report for toluene if maximum on-site inventory at any time exceeds 10,000 lbs. Report to SERC, LEPC, and local fire department by March 1. | | **Regulatory Source** | 40 CFR 370; EPCRA Section 312 | | **Applicability** | **YES – OBLIGATION TRIGGERED**
• Toluene is an OSHA hazardous chemical
• Threshold: **10,000 lbs** at any one time
• Annual usage of 28,000 lbs strongly suggests threshold exceeded; must verify maximum storage quantity | | **ISO 14001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Emergency preparedness environmental aspects) | | **ISO 45001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Emergency response planning) | | **Evaluation (9.1.2)** | **How:** Review chemical purchase orders, storage tank capacities, and safety data sheets to determine peak on-site quantity. Document maximum daily inventory.
**When:** **Annually by January 31** to prepare March 1 submission; re-evaluate whenever storage practices or order volumes change. | --- ### **Obligation 3: OSHA Air Contaminants Standard – Toluene Exposure Limits** | Element | Details | |---------|---------| | **Requirement** | Ensure employee exposure to toluene vapor does not exceed Permissible Exposure Limits (PEL): **200 ppm TWA** (8-hr), **300 ppm STEL** (15-min), with a **500 ppm peak** (10-minute maximum). Implement engineering controls, work practices, and air monitoring. | | **Regulatory Source** | 29 CFR 1910.1000 (Table Z-2) | | **Applicability** | **YES – OBLIGATION TRIGGERED**
• Evaporation during application and curing creates inhalation hazard
• 18 employees in coating operations have potential exposure
• Initial exposure assessment required | | **ISO 14001 Clause** | N/A (Occupational health issue) | | **ISO 45001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Legal requirements for hazardous substances) | | **Evaluation (9.1.2)** | **How:** Conduct initial industrial hygiene air monitoring (personal breathing zone and area samples) during typical coating operations. Repeat monitoring when processes change or exposures approach PEL. Maintain exposure records per 29 CFR 1910.1020.
**When:** **Initial assessment immediately**; re-evaluate **annually** or after process/equipment changes, ventilation modifications, or if exposure data indicates levels >50% of PEL. | --- ### **Obligation 4: OSHA Hazard Communication Standard** | Element | Details | |---------|---------| | **Requirement** | Maintain written hazard communication program; ensure toluene containers are labeled, safety data sheets (SDS) are accessible, and employees are trained on toluene hazards (flammability, neurotoxicity, reproductive effects). | | **Regulatory Source** | 29 CFR 1910.1200 | | **Applicability** | **YES – OBLIGATION TRIGGERED**
• Toluene is a hazardous chemical per OSHA definition
• All 18 employees require training | | **ISO 14001 Clause** | N/A | | **ISO 45001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Hazard communication and worker training) | | **Evaluation (9.1.2)** | **How:** Audit SDS files for current toluene supplier sheets; inspect container labeling; review training records for completion and content adequacy; interview employees for comprehension.
**When:** **Annually**; also upon new chemical introduction, new hire onboarding, process change, or SDS revision (within 30 days). | --- ### **Obligation 5: RCRA – Hazardous Waste Determination & Management** | Element | Details | |---------|---------| | **Requirement** | Determine if toluene waste streams (spent solvents, contaminated rags, filters, still bottoms) are hazardous waste (likely F005 listed waste and/or D001 ignitable waste). Manage under generator rules (SQG/LQG), including manifesting, storage time limits, and reporting. | | **Regulatory Source** | 40 CFR 262; Indiana state rules (329 IAC 3.1) | | **Applicability** | **YES – OBLIGATION TRIGGERED**
• Toluene is a listed hazardous waste (F005) when spent
• Ignitable waste characteristic (D001) applies (flash point 40°F)
• Waste generation rate must be quantified to determine generator category | | **ISO 14001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Waste management compliance) | | **ISO 45001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Hazardous waste handling safety) | | **Evaluation (9.1.2)** | **How:** Conduct waste characterization for each waste stream containing toluene. Track monthly waste generation quantities to determine generator status (VSQG: <220 lbs/month; SQG: 220-2,200 lbs/month; LQG: >2,200 lbs/month). Inspect storage areas and manifest records.
**When:** **Quarterly** waste generation reviews; **annual** comprehensive compliance audit; immediate re-evaluation if waste volumes or processes change. | --- ### **Obligation 6: Clean Air Act – VOC Emissions & NESHAP Applicability** | Element | Details | |---------|---------| | **Requirement** | Determine applicability of **NESHAP Subpart MMMMM** (Surface Coating of Miscellaneous Metal Parts). If applicable, meet VOC content limits, work practice standards, and reporting requirements. Obtain required air permit from Indiana IDEM. | | **Regulatory Source** | 40 CFR 63 Subpart MMMMM; Indiana Air Rules (326 IAC) | | **Applicability** | **MAYBE – REQUIRES FURTHER ANALYSIS**
• Must calculate facility's potential to emit (PTE) from 28,000 lbs toluene (~4,200 lbs VOC emissions) plus other coatings
• Subpart MMMMM applies if facility is a "major source" (≥10 tons/year HAP or ≥100 tons/year VOC) or part of a larger "major source"
• Indiana state permit may be required even for minor sources | | **ISO 14001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Air emissions compliance) | | **ISO 45001 Clause** | N/A (unless combustion safety) | | **Evaluation (9.1.2)** | **How:** Calculate annual VOC and HAP emissions using mass balance or AP-42 factors. Compare to regulatory thresholds. Review IDEM source classification guidance.
**When:** **Immediately** for applicability determination; **annually** thereafter; re-evaluate if coating usage increases by >10% or new products added. | --- ### **Obligation 7: Indiana Fire Code – Flammable Liquid Storage** | Element | Details | |---------|---------| | **Requirement** | Comply with flammable liquid storage, handling, and fire code requirements for toluene (Class IB flammable liquid). Includes storage cabinet requirements, ventilation, bonding/grounding, and fire suppression. | | **Regulatory Source** | Indiana Fire Code (675 IAC 22) adopting NFPA 30 Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code | | **Applicability** | **YES – OBLIGATION TRIGGERED**
• Toluene is Class IB flammable liquid
• Bulk storage and use in coating operations triggers requirements | | **ISO 14001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Emergency preparedness) | | **ISO 45001 Clause** | 6.1.3 (Fire and explosion hazards) | | **Evaluation (9.1.2)** | **How:** Inspect storage tanks/containers for UL listing, grounding, ventilation, and separation distances. Review fire department inspection records. Verify employee training on flammable liquid handling.
**When:** **Quarterly** inspections; **annual** fire code compliance audit; after any storage configuration change. | --- ## **Immediate Action Items** 1. **TRI Retroactive Filing:** Engage environmental consultant immediately to file overdue TRI reports for prior years (potential 5-year lookback). EPA penalty policy: Up to $37,500 per day per violation. 2. **Tier II Filing:** Prepare and submit 2024 Tier II report by March 1, 2024 (if not already filed) and confirm 2025 filing. 3. **Air Monitoring:** Conduct toluene exposure assessment within 30 days to establish baseline and ensure worker protection. 4. **Waste Audit:** Characterize all toluene-related waste streams and verify generator status within 60 days. 5. **Emissions Calculation:** Calculate facility-wide VOC emissions to determine CAA permit applicability. ## **ISO 9.1.2 Compliance Evaluation Summary** | Obligation | Evaluation Frequency | Method | Records | |------------|---------------------|--------|---------| | TRI Reporting | Annual (by March 1) | Usage tracking vs. 10,000-lb threshold | Purchase logs, inventory sheets, Form R | | Tier II | Annual (by Jan 31) | Max inventory review | Storage records, SDS | | OSHA PEL | Initial + Annual | Air monitoring data | IH reports, exposure records | | HazCom | Annual | SDS/label/training audit | Training records, inspection logs | | RCRA | Quarterly + Annual | Waste characterization | Waste manifests, generator reports | | CAA NESHAP | Annual | Emissions calculations | PTE calculations, permit records | | Fire Code | Quarterly + Annual | Storage inspections | Inspection checklists, fire dept. reports | **Note:** All obligations should be reviewed during the annual management review (ISO 14001/45001 Clause 9.3) and after any significant operational changes.
